- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.0), model tends to under-forecast; increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.3), model often over-forecasts; reduce forecast by 1–2% to reflect bearish pressure.  
- Model consistently overestimates prices after sharp upward spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days); apply a 1–3 day lag correction to smooth out overshoot.  
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, model often fails to anticipate reversal; add 0.5–1.5% upward adjustment to counteract overcorrection.  
- For 30-day horizon, model underperforms in high volatility periods (sentiment ±0.2 or above); increase forecast by 1–3% to account for momentum carry.  
- If sentiment is neutral (±0.1) and price is trending, model often misses the direction; use sentiment as a directional filter to adjust forecast slope.
